questions.q: According to the summary, where does legendary customer service begin?
a: With taking outstanding care of employees
With offering the lowest prices on the market
With heavy spending on advertising and promotions
With hiring managers from competing companies
questions.why: The first lesson says legendary service starts inside the company: care for your staff and they will care for your clients.

questions.q: What happens when customers feel genuinely valued?
a: They stay loyal and recommend the brand to others
They expect a discount on every later purchase
They stop comparing the brand with competitors
They overlook any bad experience that follows
questions.why: The summary says valued clients become loyal and promote the brand to friends and family, helping the business flourish.

questions.q: In the clothing store example, how does the model employee behave?
a: Asks about the occasion and offers matching shoes
Waits at the register until the customer asks for help
Points the customer toward the cheapest dress in stock
Calls the manager to handle the fitting room
questions.why: The employee greets the woman, asks what the occasion is, explores options and anticipates that she may need shoes.

questions.q: Why does the summary recommend actively collecting customer feedback?
a: Knowing what customers expect makes it easier to keep them loyal
It supplies material for the company's advertising campaigns
It shows which employees should be let go
It removes the need to train staff in listening
questions.why: The third lesson says you must learn what customers expect, including negative feedback, so you can meet those expectations.

questions.q: What does the summary say about a single bad customer experience?
a: It can wipe out the customer's memory of all the good ones
It matters far less than the price the customer paid
It disappears as soon as the company apologizes
It only affects customers who complain in public
questions.why: The summary warns that a single poor experience can erase a customer's memory of every good one.
